newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles lower as May expires.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles lower as May expires.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled sharply lower in May as the Brazilians reportedly stepped in to sell the contract ahead of its expiry, market sources said.
"The Brazilians were waiting to hit it; it looks like they are going to deliver," Peter Perez, a sugar broker with Merrill Lynch, said.
The May/July spread settled at 0.18 compared with 0.29 on Tuesday's close, after July traded at a slight premium to May briefly during the session.
Dealers said trade buying narrowed the spread from around 0.20 to even.
Floor sources noted very little outright activity in the most-active contract. "It's all in the switches," Perez said.
July settled 0.07 cent weaker at 10.96 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.09 to 10.92 cents. Spot May closed down 0.18 at 11.14, having traded from 11.45 to 10.95 cents.
The back months ended 0.03 to 0.09 weaker.
Volume was estimated at 32,430 lots compared with Tuesday's official 25,512 lots.

Support was seen at 10.91 cents basis July, the low hit on April 18. Floor sources expect a move under 10.90 to set off sell stops and possibly pressure the contract to 10.77 cents, the low reached on April 17.
Brazil released its 1997/98 crop plan earlier today. The plan put output at 13.48 million tonnes, of which 5.39 tonnes would be available for export.
Production was put at 13.68 million tonnes in the 1996/97 crop, and total exports at 5.2 million tonnes.
Analysts said the numbers had been largely expected.
((-- S. Rostler, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
